user_turns:
<user_query>
Pressure-test a business thesis with maximum honesty. Be blunt. Do not cheerlead. MAG is a local sovereign agent stack that cache-mines cheap inference: a frozen byte-stable instruction prefix rides multiple provider lanes at ~96.93% cache hit; cached input is 5-31x cheaper than fresh (GLM 4.5-air $0.03/M cached, DeepSeek $0.007/M cached off-peak vs $0.22 miss); it steers cheap models with per-vendor tuned system prompts (CL4R1T4S corpus + distilled seat profiles) so they answer closer to frontier. Thesis: we are a 'distributed generator' like rooftop solar feeding the grid - we generate competent inference at near-zero marginal cost and sell the capacity. Answer exactly three things, numbered: (1) Is 'sell the generation layer' (BYOK: customer pastes their own provider key, we charge flat for the optimization stack) the right first product, vs 'feed the grid' (hosted resale at 50% of list)? Pick one and defend it. (2) Is renting a Vast.ai GPU (~$0.25-0.80/hr for 48GB, open Apache-2.0 weights, ~$2-6/M self-hosted, NO provider ToS wall) the right cheap test of the serving loop? Note self-hosting LOSES to cache-mined APIs on input cost but wins on output-heavy work, control, and legality. Is it the right first experiment or a distraction? (3) What is the single thing we are missing that kills this business if we don't see it now? Facts: output tokens are never cache-discounted ($4.4/M on GLM-5.3); z.ai ToS prohibits account sharing and restricts the coding plan to
last_assistant:
1. **BYOK.** Hosted resale at 50% of list is not a product, it is a ToS violation with inverted unit economics. Z.ai’s coding plan is personal-use, no account sharing, no resale, no proxy, no SaaS wrap, and quota is locked to supported tools — that is the cheap “plant,” and it is legally unsellable. DeepSeek’s own API already prices at or below third-party hosts; you cannot undercut the official meter and keep a 50% list discount. Worst: output is never cache-discounted. Sell GLM-5.3 at 50% of $4.4/M and you pay $4.4 while collecting $2.2; you lose money on every generated token, which is the only token that *is* generation. The 5–31× input discount lives on a frozen prefix on *one* account. Multiplex it and you are account-sharing. BYOK is the only first SKU that does not require you to own capacity you do not own: customer pays the provider, you charge a flat fee for prefix discipline, lane routing, and seat prompts. That is a small, crowded software sale (Continue, Cline, LiteLLM, OpenRouter, Portkey), not a power plant — but it is the only legal way to learn if anyone will pay for the optimizer.

2. **Distraction.** A rented Vast box is a diesel genset billed by the hour, not rooftop solar. Idle time is the whole bill; $0.25–0.80/hr at realistic 32B Q4 throughput lands ~$2–6/M blended, which already loses to DeepSeek Flash output ($0.66/M off-peak) and only sometimes beats GLM-5.3 output ($4.4/M). Mag’s claimed moat is cache-mined *input* on provider APIs. Self-hosting tests the opposite cost curve, plus you already have the serving loop on local Ollama. Vast answers a different company (“we run Apache-2.0 weights, no ToS wall”). That is a $20–50 legality probe later, not the first experiment. The first experiment is MAX_DISTILL: if RAR is not high, there is no competent cheap generation to serve on anyone’s GPU.

3. **You are metering the wiring and selling it as electricity.** 96.93% cache hit is an input-accounting artifact of a frozen prefix on *your* harness, on *your* keys.
